results.title: Does Dodd-Frank affect OTC transaction costs and liquidity? Evidence from real-time CDS trade reports - ScienceDirect
results.content:
Title: Does Dodd-Frank affect OTC transaction costs and liquidity? Evidence from real-time CDS trade reports - ScienceDirect
This paper examines transaction costs and liquidity in the index CDS market by matching intraday quotes to real-time trade reports made available through the Dodd-Frank reforms. In this paper, using real-time trade reports made available by post-financial crisis reforms, we examine the trading costs and liquidity of index credit default swaps (CDSs), an important class of OTC derivatives.3 More importantly, the richness of the disseminated trade reports allows us to analyze how different aspects of regulatory reforms are changing the landscape and thus, the liquidity of the once opaque OTC derivatives market. (Markit), to calculate transaction-level relative effective spread and other liquidity measures.4 We find substantial trading activity in the index CDS market. The average relative effective spread is about 0.27% of price level or 2.73% of CDS spread, which is in line with the transaction costs reported in other derivatives markets such as the options market.5 Moreover, we find that liquidity varies considerably across different families of index CDSs and liquidity is much higher for on-the-run series and the most popular 5-year tenor. According to the literature, reporting privately negotiated bilateral deals to SDRs represents a major improvement in market transparency in the hitherto opaque CDS market, and public dissemination of key trade information such as price and volume can lower transaction costs and improve liquidity (e.g., Pagano and Roell, 1996, Naik et al., 1999, Bessembinder and Maxwell, 2008, Acharya et al., 2009). Using data from the pre-Dodd-Frank period, we find that the initiation of real-time reporting and public dissemination of OTC swap trades are indeed associated with transaction cost reductions and liquidity improvements for index CDS contracts. In addition to transaction price and size, the disseminated trade reports provide a rich set of trade characteristics that capture different aspects of regulatory reform.8 We use these deal characteristics to evaluate a number of hypotheses relating different aspects of Dodd-Frank regulations to liquidity. (For brevity, the results of these robustness checks are not presented in the paper, but are available upon request.) First, while the first year of the Dodd-Frank regulatory regime provides the most critical time period for evaluating the impact of regulatory reforms, it is also interesting to see if the relations between various Dodd-Frank deal characteristics and index CDS transaction costs and liquidity.

results.title: Druggable targets for Parkinson’s disease: transcriptomics based Mendelian randomization study - PMC
results.content: Then, Mendelian randomization (MR) and summary statistics-based MR (SMR) analysis were conducted using eQTL data from both brain tissue and blood to investigate the relationship between gene expression and PD. Through MR and SMR analysis, P2RX7 and RNASET2 were identified as feasible PD therapeutic targets, which were highly expressed in PD tissues and increased as the Braak stages increased. MR analysis has gained momentum in repurposing approved drugs21 and identifying new treatment targets by integrating summary data from disease GWASs and expression quantitative trait locus (eQTL) studies22. Therefore, in the study, we analyzed transcriptome sequencing data of PD, and then used the summary-level data from GWAS and eQTL studies to estimate the causal effects of druggable genes on PD using a systematic druggable transcriptome-wide MR method, which can prioritize therapeutic targets for PD. The SMR, which integrates summary-level data from GWAS as well as data from eQTL studies to pinpoint genes whose expression levels contribute to complex traits due to pleiotropy, and the heterogeneity in dependent instruments test (HEIDI) that uses all SNPs in the cis-regulatory regions region to sets apart pleiotropy from linkage effect, were both used in this study to verify the conclusion of MR41. To perform phenome-wide MR examining the potential side effects of these previously identified druggable genes, eQTLs of candidate gene expression were used as exposure and summary-level data of systematically classified diseases from the UK Biobank were used as outcomes (). The results of SMR and HEIDI tests show the association between druggable gene expression from the brain tissue and PD. Through the previous analysis, the MR and SMR results of brain tissue eQTLs collected from PsychENCODE and GTEx consortia supported P2RX7 and RNASET2 as feasible PD therapeutic targets. In this study, we based on a transcriptome-based MR study to identify therapeutic targets for PD, our findings revealed 313 differentially expressed genes that were directly targetable and may have an impact on PD outcomes. Through MR and SMR analysis, we identified P2RX7 and RNASET2 as feasible PD therapeutic targets, which were highly expressed in PD tissues and increased as the Braak stages increased.
